title: Causal memory: writable matter, active questions and finite event algebra
summary: A pass through the recent memory/interrogation line. It follows writable media from GelatinIsland into JelloBrain, audits the old PerceptionLab feedback loop, tracks SighImageSuper's recoverability view of memory into active dendritic experiment design and bounded behavioral-update guards, and records CausalHorizon's exact event-space identity as a mathematical convergence point rather than an ancestry claim.

nodes.claim: A spatial excitable medium where local carriers write slow material, material routes later signals, and receiver state separately gates arrival effectiveness.
nodes.survived: Under a frozen-material matched probe, the grown spatial arrangement transmitted farther than a shuffled copy in all six reported Estuary seeds; the route × primer factorization also cleanly separates path limitation from receiver receptivity.
nodes.killed: The geometry result is not useful learning, intelligence, a validated neuron, or evidence that biological signaling uses the exact primer/material equations.

nodes.claim: Extends the gel substrate into persistent order codes, pair-specific signaling conventions, negative-image route repair, separate novelty/relevance states and failure-gated structural consolidation.
nodes.survived: Ordered traffic writes spatial operator geometry; meaningless pulses can acquire pair-specific repairable roles; prediction error can expose alternatives hidden by inherited routes; familiar-but-relevant events remain publishable; and failure-gated plasticity stabilizes two competing routes after the controller is removed.
nodes.killed: Inherited geometry can masquerade as learning, naive exploration and reward-every-success fail, fast expectation is not itself the problem, and repeated contingency reversal still breaks on representational interference in the shared scalar sheet.

nodes.claim: Uses a recursive image operator as a laboratory for asking which distinctions between past events remain recoverable, where history is carried, which query reveals it, and how retrieval changes the substrate.
nodes.survived: Memory is broader than slow eigenmodes: an eight-cell nilpotent chain carries finite temporal history, AB versus BA teaching survives exact fast-state erasure in changed material, and active query geometry can reveal a distinction invisible to a passive readout. Private interventions can also help separate self-caused from external effects.
nodes.killed: The late float16 spectral re-expansion is a quantization artifact, the transient singular spectrum is not literally a collapsing observability Gramian, and an eigenvalue-only account misses travelling and material memory.

nodes.claim: Freezes and re-audits the PerceptionLab ECG-like feedback graph that helped start the later Geometric Neuron line.
nodes.survived: The old graph contains a defensible closed-loop observation result: changing the image-vector resolution changes the spatial measurement operator inside feedback, which changes the future trajectory generated by the controller.
nodes.killed: The first four feedback values were not four Fourier/eigen modes; they were the first four spatial samples of a resolution-dependent resized image, so the older eigenmode story is explicitly corrected.

nodes.claim: Turns the active-question idea into a bounded experiment-design problem: choose physically realizable stimulation that separates plausible hidden dendritic changes from nuisance, model mismatch and calibration drift at limited recording sites.
nodes.survived: Symmetry can make a real hidden change exactly invisible to one stimulation and visible to another; nuisance-aware fixed stimulation panels beat controlled random designs in the harder toy; paired baseline measurement and a compressed empirical transfer fingerprint are useful resources; ambiguity is reported rather than hidden.
nodes.killed: The original ~99% localization result was largely unique stimulation coding, the first planner overvalued tiny separations, and the first adaptive planner did not beat the strong fixed Gate-4 design; current seven-way top-1 accuracy remains modest.

nodes.claim: Builds a bounded behavioral-update guard: proposed changes are measured against remembered queries, finite candidate effects are checked before commitment, and replay/reference coverage is treated as a resource rather than a free oracle.
nodes.survived: The software guard can preserve declared old-response bounds while improving a new response; measured nonlinear compensation repairs a concrete failure of first-order preservation; partial-cue tests expose that preserving full answers is not the same as preserving access to them.
nodes.killed: A finite reference bank does not certify unseen behavior, informed replay has not established an unseen-access advantage, added capacity did not help the tested mixed-cue benchmark, and temporary candidate evaluation is a software privilege rather than a biological mechanism.

nodes.claim: States an exact finite-rank identity for time-ordered linear propagators with ordered low-rank event edits, exposing event-event interaction through a finite nilpotent event-space resolvent and an observer-dependent algebraic interaction horizon.
nodes.survived: The finite-event identity, rank bound, exact pair-interference term, observer projection and finite polynomial interaction-depth expansion are algebraically explicit and numerically verified to about 2.7e-15 worst relative error over the initial random test battery.
nodes.killed: The repository does not claim historical priority, nonlinear generality, a brain mechanism, or that the motivating nonlinear repositories must obey the same factorization; the prior projects are explicitly labeled motivation only.

motifs.title: Memory is a distinction a later question can still recover
motifs.description: SighImageSuper makes the definition explicit across lingering, travelling and material carriers; JelloBrain writes distinctions into spatial material; IttnasNoruen asks which old behavioral distinctions remain protected under updates; CausalHorizon factors the linear case into event entry, internal interaction and observer projection.

motifs.title: The question can change the system being observed
motifs.description: The re-audited PerceptionLab loop places measurement inside feedback; SighImageSuper studies query back-action; Active Dendrite turns the choice of stimulation/operating condition into experiment design; IttnasNoruen charges the cost of temporary candidate interrogation before a write is committed.

motifs.title: History becomes operator geometry
motifs.description: GelatinIsland and JelloBrain let traffic write slow routing material; Operaattori compiles physical structure into response; SighImageSuper shows teaching can change later query geometry even after fast state is erased; Active Dendrite asks which experiment reveals that changed structure.

motifs.title: Static proximity is weaker than propagated causal overlap
motifs.description: Kompressori finds overlap-dependent interference in operator responses; CausalHorizon isolates the exact directed propagated overlap Omega_ji for low-rank linear event edits and proposes it as the next measurable handoff back to Kompressori.
